title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 9-11): a 'tranchée' L is a totally ordered set, apparently dense in the relevant cases (the next page invokes 'divisibilité' of 'binaire' tranchées). It can be a segment, a half-interval or an interval, and its boundary ∂L is the set of its extremal elements. Grothendieck attaches to L a combinatorial complex. S_0(L) = Drap_2(L) is the set of 2-element chains {x<y}. Modf(L) = Drap(L) is the set of finite chains, i.e. the order complex (flag complex) of L.

This page: for a simplex S in Modf(L) he defines C(S) = {l ∈ L : l ∉ S, S∪{l} a chain}. This is the vertex set of the link of S in the order complex. Since L is totally ordered, C(S) = L∖S.

Writing S = {s_1<...<s_n}, the 'connected components' of C(S) are the non-empty sets among L_{<s_1}, ]s_1,s_2[, ..., ]s_{n-1},s_n[, L_{>s_n}. The cases are:
- n = 0: a single component, L itself.
- n = 1: the components L_{<s} and L_{>s}, those that are non-empty.
- By density, the inner open intervals are non-empty. The only possibly empty pieces are L_{<s_1} (empty exactly when s_1 is the least element) and L_{>s_n} (empty exactly when s_n is the greatest element).

The boundaries of the components are {s_1}, {s_1,s_2}, ..., {s_{n-1},s_n}, {s_n}, the outer ones only when the component exists. So L with its finite subsets behaves like a combinatorial 1-dimensional 'tame' space: points cut it into open arcs whose boundaries are 0- or 2-point sets.

The page ends by announcing a claim. The 'bicoloured structure of triangles' (hence the whole structure (a)(b)(c) of the 'découpage'/'réseau' formalism of the chapter) should be recoverable from structure (a) alone, plus (b) for T ∈ S_0, i.e. for edges.

The next page starts the proof with a lemma: an order up to reversal ('biordonnée') is determined by the ternary betweenness relation R(a,b,c), meaning a<b<c or a>b>c. Comparability/disjointness is then characterised via the existence of an element strictly between, using density. The purpose is an axiomatic, order-theoretic description of 1-dimensional cells in a combinatorial theory of cellular decompositions ('réseaux via découpages').
errors: No mathematical error. The condition 'S∪{l} tot. ord.' in C(S) is vacuous for a totally ordered L; it is only meaningful in the more general poset setting, which suggests the definition is copied from a general framework.
The claim that the inner intervals ]s_i,s_{i+1}[ are non-empty requires L to be dense. This is not stated on the page but is assumed (cf. 'divisibilité' on p.11).

ideas.what: Finite chains of a totally ordered set as a simplicial complex (Drap(L) = Modf(L)), with S_0 = 2-chains
ideas.modern_name: order complex / flag complex of a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Alexandroff; order complex standard in combinatorial topology, e.g. Quillen 1978, Björner)

ideas.what: C(S) = vertices compatible with S, decomposed into connected components (open intervals) with boundaries {s_i,s_{i+1}} or {s_1},{s_n}
ideas.modern_name: link of a simplex; complement of a finite set in a dense linear order as a union of open intervals (cell decomposition in dimension 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; in tame topology the 1-dimensional o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, mid-1980s)

ideas.what: Recovering the full structure (a)(b)(c) (bicoloured triangles) from structure (a) plus (b) on edges
ideas.modern_name: reduction of axioms of a combinatorial cellular structure to lower-dimensional data

ideas.what: (next page) A linear order up to reversal is determined by the ternary betweenness relation

missed.claim: Grothendieck models 1-dimensional 'tame' cells purely order-theoretically: a dense linear order, cut by finite sets into open intervals with explicit boundaries. In 1986 this parallels the then-new o-minimal cell decomposition, which he does not cite and probably did not know. It is part of his own programme of 'découpages' (cf. Esquisse, topologie modérée). The page itself is elementary; the interest lies only in documenting how he built the combinatorial foundation.
missed.quote: Les comp. connexes sont les ens. non vides parmi L_{<s_1}, ]s_1,s_2[, ..., ]s_{n-1},s_n[, L_{>s_n}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical interest for the relation between Grothendieck's tame-topology programme and o-minimality. There is no new mathematics on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary bookkeeping on finite chains in a dense linear order (order complex, links, components). The only non-routine item is the announced reduction of the bicoloured-triangle structure to structure (a) plus edge data, which is internal to his unpublished formalism and is only stated, not proved, here.
transcription_corrections: 'Les seules non vides éventuellement étant' should mathematically read 'Les seules vides éventuellement étant' (L_{<s_1} is empty iff s_1 is the least element; L_{>s_n} is empty iff s_n is the greatest). The handwriting before 'vides' is unclear.
'ou n≥2 : voir ci-dessus plus haut' is probably 'voir ce qui est plus haut'.
In the line 'on a donc C(S)=', the struck-out word before 'l ∉ S' appears to be a cancelled 'S∪{l}'.
